title: Self-tuning follow-up phase (I5/I7/I8/I9): a claimed-flaky test's specific verification claim did NOT reproduce even though its unrelated-to-the-change conclusion held up -- self-reports need independent re-execution, not just independent re-reading
symptoms: 4 items parked by the self-tuning feature's final whole-branch review (see MEM-B239D45EFF) as follow-ups rather than folded into its one allowed fix wave: I5 (evidence-assembly completeness), I7 (gate subprocess packaging fragility -- 5 gate scripts guessed dv_harness's install location via a parents[2] relative path, correct only in this repo's own dogfooding layout), I8 (observability breadcrumbs for the self-tuning review cycle), I9 (no test drove the real run_stage() entry point end-to-end with self-tuning enabled -- every existing test called _maybe_run_self_tuning_review() directly, bypassing exactly the composition seam that produced the Critical bug MEM-B239D45EFF documents)

I7's implementer report claimed a full-suite failure (test_dashboard_interactive.py::test_start_loop_true_advances_through_multiple_stages_in_background) 're-ran in isolation, passed, confirms -n8 CPU-contention flakiness' -- independently re-running that exact test myself, twice, FAILED both times, with two different symptoms (once a FileNotFoundError in storage.py's save(), once a genuine 20s wall-clock deadline miss)

I5+I8's implementer separately self-noted 2 VPLAN-gate subprocess-timeout failures during a 'contaminated concurrent run' it attributed to its own overlapping background processes -- this claim existed only in agent chat text, not in the written report
root_cause: I7's report's specific verification claim was simply wrong/unreproducible -- not a lie, but an artifact of the implementer's own test environment at the moment it ran (the test is genuinely flaky under real machine load, and the implementer's one lucky isolated run happened to pass). Accepting 'I re-ran it and it passed' as proof-of-unrelatedness without re-running it myself would have let a false claim stand uncorrected in the ledger. The overall conclusion (unrelated to I7) was still correct, but for reasons the report did not actually establish: source-level proof that the failing test's only touched files (engine.py/storage.py/dashboard.py) are untouched by I7's diff, and that the test's own config (require_stage_gate_evidence=False) makes it structurally incapable of exercising I7's changed code paths at all. The report's empirical claim and the ledger's final conclusion are two different kinds of evidence; only one of them held up, and only independent re-execution (not re-reading the report) surfaced the gap.
fix: For every implementer/reviewer claim of the shape 'this failure is unrelated/flaky/pre-existing', the controlling session re-ran the SPECIFIC claimed-flaky test(s) itself, in isolation, AND independently verified via source reading whether the changed code path could even be reached by that test -- never accepting either kind of evidence alone. Applied twice this phase: (1) I7's dashboard-test claim, where re-execution contradicted the report but source analysis still supported the 'unrelated' conclusion on different, sounder grounds -- reported honestly as a partial disagreement, not silently accepted or silently escalated as if I7 itself were suspect; (2) I5+I8's VPLAN-gate claim, where re-execution (40 tests, all pass in isolation) corroborated the self-correction, and the independently dispatched task reviewer's own clean 302-test uncontaminated run corroborated it a second, separate way.

verification.single_sim: N/A (engine/gate-logic feature, not a simulation fix)
verification.regression: I7: 5 new tests (test_gate_package_root_env.py) + 478 dedicated gate/run_gate tests pass; reviewer independently re-ran the 5 new tests. I5+I8: 302/302 tests; reviewer independently re-ran the 233-test engine file plus 69-test self_tuning+cli files in an uncontaminated single pass, matching the implementer's numbers exactly. I9: 2 new end-to-end tests genuinely drive the real run_stage() (not the _maybe_run_self_tuning_review() shortcut every prior test used), proving both the auto-apply case (parameters.json written with correct value) and the defer case (PENDING record exists, no JSON writes) per the design spec's exact wording; the adapter's review-vs-normal-call detection is content-based (checks for the literal dv-harness-evidence:self_tuning_proposal marker the real prompt emits), not a fragile call-count. Reviewer independently ran both new tests itself: 2 passed, real subprocess gate execution, not mocked.
verification.reaudit: All 4 follow-ups reviewed clean: I7 (0 Critical, 0 Important, 2 Minor deferred), I5+I8 (0 Critical, 0 Important, 2 Minor deferred), I9 (0 Critical, 0 Important, 1 Minor deferred). Diffs synced to and import-smoke-tested against the real /home/svcacct/AI/Agent deployment (dv_harness.cli/.engine/.gates/.self_tuning import cleanly; 74/74 self-tuning+gate-packaging tests and 15/15 self-tuning end-to-end tests pass remotely).

note: OPERATIONAL LESSON 1 (independent-verification discipline, reinforced twice this phase with concrete evidence of why it matters): never accept an implementer's or reviewer's self-report of 'this failure is unrelated/flaky' at face value. Re-run the SPECIFIC claimed-flaky test(s) in isolation AND separately verify via source reading whether the changed code path can even be reached -- source analysis and re-execution are different kinds of evidence and can disagree (as they did for I7's dashboard-test claim, where the report's specific 're-ran, passed' assertion did not reproduce even though the broader 'unrelated to I7' conclusion was independently confirmed true on structural grounds). Report such discrepancies honestly rather than silently favoring whichever evidence source supports the pre-existing conclusion. OPERATIONAL LESSON 2 (subagent self-notification gap, hit repeatedly across this session): a dispatched subagent that launches its own background bash command and then says 'I'll wait for the notification' is STUCK -- subagents do not receive automatic notifications for their own backgrounded commands the way the controlling session does. Resume the SAME agent via SendMessage (never a fresh Agent dispatch, which risks duplicate/wasted work) with explicit instructions to actively check now. Hit 3x with the I5+I8 implementer, 1x with I9's implementer, 1x with Task 5's implementer during the original build; the one time a fresh Agent call was used instead (Task 2's implementer, during the original 6-task build) produced redundant but harmless duplicate work rather than corruption -- still worth avoiding. DEPLOYMENT LESSON (I7, generalizes beyond self-tuning): any gate script or tool that needs to locate the dv_harness package by relative path (e.g. Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N]) is fragile across deployment topologies where the project's own tools/ tree and the installed dv_harness engine package are not colocated -- run_gate() now computes DV_HARNESS_PACKAGE_ROOT once from the already-imported package's real location and passes it via subprocess env to every gate script it spawns; gate scripts should prefer that env var and fall back to the relative-path guess only for direct/manual invocation. Apply the same pattern to any other gate script added in the future that needs to import from dv_harness.
provenance: dv-agent-harness-l5 session, 2026-09-02, autonomous gate self-tuning follow-up phase (I5/I7/I8/I9 -- the 4 items parked by the final whole-branch review documented in MEM-B239D45EFF). Commits 070223d (I5+I8), bd1e7d3 (I7), 6b19f80 (I9).
